questions.question: Insulin and epidermal growth factor (EGF) act through which type of receptor?
questions.explanation: Insulin, EGF, and many other growth factors act through receptor tyrosine kinases: hormone binding causes receptor dimerization, activating an intracellular tyrosine kinase domain that autophosphorylates and triggers downstream signalling — a process that plays out over minutes to hours, much slower than ion-channel receptors.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.sourceChapter: Mechanism of Drug Action; Receptor Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: A therapist begins prosthetic training activities for a patient with a transtibial amputation. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial activity?
questions.explanation: Weight shifting in standing (to learn loading the prosthesis) is the first step of transtibial prosthetic training.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A therapist revises the results of ultraviolet testing. Which grade of erythemal dose best describe the time required for mold reddening of the skin?
questions.explanation: The minimal erythema dose produces mild reddening.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: If the size of the electrode is small, the current density will be ______ and the perception of the stimulus will be ______.
questions.explanation: Small electrodes give a high density and a stronger sensation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: On ECG, leads II, III and aVF correspond to the ______ wall of the heart.
questions.explanation: These leads look at the inferior wall (right coronary artery territory).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Which of the following spontaneous activities is considered normal on EMG?
questions.explanation: End-plate noise and spikes are normal findings during needle insertion near the motor point.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The normal protein content of CSF in an adult is:
questions.explanation: CSF protein is normally 15-45 mg/dL; it rises in meningitis and GBS.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A hyperextended (recurvatum) knee during stance suggests:
questions.explanation: Patients with a weak quadriceps lock the knee back to stand.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: When the p-value is less than the alpha value, the null hypothesis is:
questions.explanation: A significant result rejects the null hypothesis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: When a test shows consistency by multiple raters, it is ______ reliability.
questions.explanation: Inter-rater reliability measures agreement between different examiners.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Which studies are employed to describe the occurrence of an outcome?
questions.explanation: Descriptive studies document who, where and when.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: In the slump test, adding hip abduction with flexion to 90 degrees places maximum tension on the:
questions.explanation: Hip abduction in the slump test biases the obturator nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A minimal tear of the anterior talofibular ligament is graded as ankle sprain:
questions.explanation: Grade 1: stretch or minimal tear of the ATFL with minimal functional loss.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A recognised adverse effect of statins is:
questions.explanation: Monitor CK if symptomatic.
